purpose: Test a natural intrinsically nonsymmetric polynomially simulable candidate family after symmetric/low-rank holographic normal forms were excluded: qutrit affine-support quadratic-phase (stabilizer-type) tensors and their full independent-port GL(3,C)^6 orbit. Derive an exact cut-rank invariant rather than performing numerical orbit fitting.

candidate_class.name: QUTRIT_AFFINE_QUADRATIC_PHASE
candidate_class.definition: For n qutrit variables z in F3^n, f(z)=lambda*1[z in a+L]*omega^{Q(z)}, where lambda is nonzero complex, L is a linear F3-subspace, omega is a primitive cube root of unity, and Q:F3^n->F3 has degree at most two.
candidate_class.scope_note: This is a precisely defined qutrit stabilizer-type candidate family. The artifact does not claim that it exhausts all asymmetric tractable Holant signatures on domain three.

power_of_three_flattening_theorem.name: AFFINE_QUADRATIC_PHASE_CUT_RANK_IS_A_POWER_OF_THREE
power_of_three_flattening_theorem.statement: For every f in QUTRIT_AFFINE_QUADRATIC_PHASE and every bipartition X|Y of its variables, the complex matrix rank of the X|Y flattening is 3^r for some integer r>=0.
proof: Translations of the affine support and linear/pure-X/pure-Y terms of Q only permute rows/columns or multiply them by nonzero diagonal phases, so they do not change rank.

Let L be linear. Put K_X=L intersect (X direct-sum 0), K_Y=L intersect (0 direct-sum Y), U=pi_X(L), V=pi_Y(L). Membership in L induces a canonical isomorphism U/K_X -> V/K_Y. Therefore, after row/column permutations, the flattening is block diagonal with exactly 3^c blocks, c=dim(U/K_X).

Within every block, write x=x_0+u and y=y_0+v with u in K_X and v in K_Y. Removing nonzero row/column phase factors leaves the character matrix M_B(u,v)=omega^{B(u,v)}, where B is the X-Y bilinear part of Q restricted to K_X x K_Y.

Let beta:K_X->K_Y^* be beta(u)=B(u,·), with rank s. Rows of M_B are additive characters of K_Y. Two rows coincide exactly modulo ker(beta), while distinct characters are linearly independent. Hence rank(M_B)=|im(beta)|=3^s.
All 3^c blocks have the same rank 3^s, so the full flattening rank is 3^(c+s).
power_of_three_flattening_theorem.field_note: The proof is over C using exact F3 character orthogonality and therefore applies to arbitrary affine dimensions, not just the six-leg instance.

portwise_orbit_invariance.statement: For any independent invertible port bases G=T_1 tensor ... tensor T_n in GL(3,C)^n, every named bipartition flattening rank is invariant because the flattening is left- and right-multiplied by invertible Kronecker matrices.
portwise_orbit_invariance.consequence: Every tensor in the full portwise GL(3,C)^n orbit of an affine-quadratic-phase tensor also has power-of-three rank on every cut.

janus_local_tensor_certificate.signature: F6(k)=0 off sum_i k_i=0; on conservation F6(k)=-2+3*delta(VP dot k=0)+3*delta(VM dot k=0), VP=(1,1,0,1,1,0), VM=(1,2,0,2,0,1).

exact_cut_rank_profiles_over_Q_equals_C.2|4: 3 on 1 cut, 6 on 6 cuts, 9 on 8 cuts
exact_cut_rank_profiles_over_Q_equals_C.3|3: 6 on 4 cuts, 9 on 8 cuts, 12 on 8 cuts

janus_local_tensor_certificate.obstruction: Ranks 6 and 12 occur. Neither is a power of three. Since rank is unchanged over Q->C for this integer tensor and under any independent invertible port basis, F6 cannot lie in the GL(3,C)^6 orbit of QUTRIT_AFFINE_QUADRATIC_PHASE.

barrier_theorem.name: NO_PORTWISE_GL3_ORBIT_INTERSECTION_WITH_QUTRIT_AFFINE_QUADRATIC_PHASE_V8_5_7
barrier_theorem.statement: There do not exist invertible 3x3 complex matrices T_1,...,T_6 such that (T_1 tensor ... tensor T_6)F6 is a qutrit affine-support quadratic-phase tensor.
barrier_theorem.proof_certificate: The exact 2|4 and 3|3 ranks include 6 and 12, contradicting the power-of-three cut-rank theorem for the target class and rank invariance under GL(3,C)^6.
barrier_theorem.scope: This is not a general Holant hardness theorem. It excludes one broad stabilizer/affine-quadratic-phase holographic contraction route, including nonsymmetric members of that precisely defined class.
